\section{Sensitivity analysis (E6)}\label{sec:sens}
We varied one parameter at a time over five values on six classical and four CEC2017 functions, one per class (30 runs, 30,030 FEs; Figure~\ref{fig:sens}, Table~\ref{tab:sens}). A Friedman test across the five values of each parameter on each function, with Holm correction over \EsixCells{} tests, is significant in \EsixSigCells{} cases: \EsixSigLscout{} for $L_{\mathrm{scout}}$, \EsixSigBeta{} for the $\beta$ range, \EsixSigBounds{} for the $\phi_3$ bounds (\EsixSigFnsBounds), and \EsixSigRho{} for $\rho$, $W$ and $\delta$. % const

\paragraph{Deposit.}
$\Delta$ has no effect by construction: all \EsixDeltaTuples{} runs are identical across its five values. Pheromone is used only to compare neighbors, the initial amount decays equally for all particles, and scaling every deposit by a constant leaves the comparison unchanged. It is a redundant parameter.

\paragraph{Scout limit.}
The longest limit tested, \EsixLscoutMax, gives the best mean on \EsixLscoutBestAtMax{} of \EsixFns{} functions. Sphere improves from \EsixLSphereDefault{} at the default \EsixLscoutDefault{} to \EsixLSphereLong, and Schwefel from \EsixLSchwefelDefault{} to \EsixLSchwefelLong.
In an exploratory comparison at that limit, BeeBio is significantly better than AntBio on \EsixLongBetterAnt{} of \EsixFns{} functions and worse on \EsixLongWorseAnt. The cost of scouts reported in the main text therefore belongs to the default limit, not to scouts as such. We keep the default, as settings were frozen before these runs and choosing a limit here would tune on the test functions.

\paragraph{Contraction range.}
The $\beta$ range trades precision against exploration: ending at 0.75 instead of 0.5 takes Sphere from \EsixBetaSphereDefault{} to \EsixBetaSphereHigh{} and Rastrigin from \EsixBetaRastriginDefault{} to \EsixBetaRastriginHigh. % const

Apart from these two parameters, the results are stable, so the defaults of $\rho$, $W$, $\delta$ and the $\phi_3$ bounds are not driving the findings of the main text.

\section{Schwefel with the optimum moved inward (E7b)}\label{sec:e7b}
E7b tests a specific hypothesis: the gap to QPSO on Schwefel exists because the optimum lies near the bound. It moves the optimum inward, from $c=420.97$ to % const
$c=120.97$, with a CEC-style penalty outside the domain (Table~\ref{tab:e7b}). Under clipping, all six family members are significantly % const
worse than QPSO with the optimum near the bound (\EsevBWorseNear{} of 6), and only \EsevBWorseInward{} with the optimum inward. AntBio's ratio % const
to QPSO's mean falls from \EsevBRatioNearClipAnt{} to \EsevBRatioInwardClipAnt, and BeeBio's from \EsevBRatioNearClipBee{} to \EsevBRatioInwardClipBee.
Under reflection, however, the gap remains (AntBio \EsevBRatioNearReflectAnt{} to \EsevBRatioInwardReflectAnt), and the no-bio control stays worse inward under
both handlers (\EsevBRatioInwardClipNobio{} and \EsevBRatioInwardReflectNobio). The hypothesis is therefore supported for clipping, the handling used in the main
experiments, but rejected as a complete explanation, since part of the gap is unrelated to where the optimum lies.

\begin{sidewaystable}
\centering\tabsetup
\caption{Schwefel with the optimum near the bound (near: $c=420.97$) or moved inward (inward: $c=120.97$), by boundary handler (E7b: mean fitness, $D=30$, 30 runs, 30{,}030 FEs).}\label{tab:e7b}
\geninput{e7b_schwefel.tex}
\end{sidewaystable}

\section{The opfunu implementation: a documented discrepancy}\label{sec:official}
A first run of this study evaluated CEC2017 through the opfunu library (version 1.0.4), which numbers the functions so that its F$k$ is % const
official F$(k{+}1)$ for $k\ge2$, and whose F5 (official F6) we excluded as nearly flat, leaving 28 functions. We then compared it with the % const
official C implementation and its data files at five fixed random points in $[-100,100]^D$ per function, at $D=30$ and $D=50$. % const
Table~\ref{tab:official} gives the largest relative difference of $f-f^*$. The two agree on \CecOffSameList{} only. Loading the official
shift, rotation and shuffle data into opfunu makes \CecOffDataOnlyList{} agree as well, so for these the formula is the official one
and only the data differ. For the other functions the formula differs: for example, the Rastrigin function (opfunu F4) omits the
official scaling of $z$ by $5.12/100$, and the Zakharov function (F2) omits the index weights in its second sum. The composition functions % const
already use the official data files and still differ. All CEC2017 experiments were therefore repeated on the official code, with the same
algorithms, settings, seeds and budgets; the main text reports only those runs. The opfunu results are kept here.

\paragraph{Results on opfunu.}
The main conclusions are the same on both implementations: L-SHADE ranks first at the standard budget (opfunu: \OpEthreesThirtyRankLSHADE{} at $D=30$ and
\OpEthreesFiftyRankLSHADE{} at $D=50$), neither leader reaches the overall threshold (opfunu: ant \OpEtwocBioCountAnt, bee \OpEtwocBioCountBee{} of \OpEthreeN), and no
schedule is credited on any function. The size of some effects differs. Scouts are worse on \OpDcScoutsCeWorse{} of \OpEthreeN{} opfunu functions
but on \DcScoutsCeWorse{} of \EthreeN{} official ones, and the bee leader is credited on \OpEtwocBioCountBee{} opfunu functions but \EtwocBioCountBee{} official ones.
At the standard budget, the Holm-corrected Wilcoxon test finds \OpEthreesThirtyBioPwBetterList{} better than QPSO on opfunu at $D=30$ and
\OpEthreesFiftyBioPwBetterList{} at $D=50$; on the official suite it finds \EthreesThirtyBioPwBetterList{} at $D=30$ and \EthreesFiftyBioPwBetterList{} at $D=50$.
On opfunu, restricted to the \CecOffFormulaCount{} functions with the official formula (\CecOffFormulaList), the $D=50$ comparison has too few functions for any
Wilcoxon test on means to reach $p<0.05$. Table~\ref{tab:opranks} gives the opfunu ranks and Table~\ref{tab:opdecomp} the decomposition. % const
The CEC part of the sensitivity analysis (Section~\ref{sec:sens}) was also first run on opfunu F1, F4, F11 and F21, with the same settings; % const
there, \OpEsixSigCells{} of \OpEsixCells{} Holm-corrected Friedman tests are significant (Table~\ref{tab:opsens}). Section~\ref{sec:sens} uses the official functions.
